disease_label_per_paper: Measles confirmed by positive PCR and anti-measles IgM in an unvaccinated adult traveler with Koplik spots
presentation_summary: 42-year-old Caucasian man presented after recent travel to Brazil.
He had 3 days of fever, cough, odynophagia, and progressive skin rash appearing 10 days after return.
Immunization records showed no documented measles vaccination.
Physical examination showed a cephalocaudal maculopapular rash across face, chest, and extremities, plus multiple 1-2 mm gray-white buccal mucosal spots consistent with Koplik spots.
Oropharyngeal swab, urine, and blood specimens were collected.
Measles diagnosis was confirmed by positive PCR and serology showing anti-measles IgM titer 8.4 with IgG titer 9.0 below the positive threshold.
The patient was placed in a negative-pressure isolation room with airborne precautions and public-health measures; no onward transmission was reported.
He received supportive care and all symptoms disappeared within a few weeks.
